quiz.explain: Azure Policy evaluates resource properties such as location and denies requests that break the rule, for every caller. Choice A is tempting because RBAC controls permissions, but it decides which actions an identity can perform, not which regions a resource may be created in.

days.recap: Microsoft Purview governs data, Azure Policy enforces and audits how resources are configured with definitions, initiatives and effects, and resource locks stop deletion or changes even by Owners.

days.title: Managing and Deploying Azure: Portal, Cloud Shell, CLI, PowerShell, Azure Arc, Resource Manager, and IaC

concepts.heading: The Azure Portal and Cloud Shell
concepts.body: The Azure portal is a web-based graphical console where you create and manage resources with guided forms, view their state, and build custom dashboards, with no scripting needed. It suits learning, one-off tasks and people who prefer a visual tool. Azure Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell, opened from the portal or its own address, that offers Bash or PowerShell with the Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell already installed and signed in as you. Nothing has to be installed on your own computer. Cloud Shell runs with the signed-in user's own permissions and never grants more than their Azure RBAC roles. Its sessions run on temporary hosts: an ephemeral session needs no storage account but keeps nothing afterwards, while attaching an Azure Files share keeps your scripts and files between sessions. The exam signal for Cloud Shell is a locked-down or shared computer where nothing can be installed.

concepts.heading: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell
concepts.body: The Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell are command-line tools that manage the same Azure resources, and both can be scripted to automate repeated tasks. The Azure CLI uses commands such as az vm create and runs in many shells, including Bash, Windows command prompt and PowerShell. Azure PowerShell is a set of cmdlets, such as New-AzVM, that runs in PowerShell and passes objects between commands. Both run on Windows, Linux and macOS, and both are available in Cloud Shell. The choice is mostly about the team's skills: a Windows team already writing PowerShell scripts picks Azure PowerShell, while a Linux team used to Bash often picks the Azure CLI. For example, an engineer repeating fifteen portal steps every Monday should capture them in a script. The exam signal is automation of repeated tasks, not which tool is more powerful.

concepts.heading: Azure Resource Manager
concepts.body: Azure Resource Manager is the deployment and management service for Azure. Every request from the portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, REST API or SDKs goes through Resource Manager, which authenticates the caller, checks Azure RBAC, applies Azure Policy and resource locks, and then sends the request to the right service. That is why a VM created in the portal and one created with the CLI end up the same. Resource Manager also provides the management scopes (management groups, subscriptions, resource groups and resources), so settings applied at one scope are inherited below it, and it lets you manage, tag and delete related resources as a group. For example, deleting a resource group removes everything inside it in one action. Exam questions that ask why all tools give consistent results or apply the same access control point to Resource Manager.

concepts.heading: Infrastructure as Code: ARM Templates and Bicep
concepts.body: Infrastructure as code means describing your infrastructure in files that are versioned and reused, instead of clicking through the portal. ARM templates are JSON files that declare what you want, not the steps to build it. Resource Manager validates the template before deploying, works out the order of dependent resources and deploys independent ones in parallel. Deployments are idempotent: deploying the same template again gives the same resources in the same state. Large templates can be split into smaller linked templates and reused. Bicep is a simpler declarative language for the same purpose: it compiles to ARM template JSON, is deployed by Resource Manager, and needs no separate state file. For example, a team building identical dev, test and production environments deploys one Bicep file three times. When environments drift because people changed settings by hand, the fix is to change the code and redeploy.

concepts.heading: Azure Arc
concepts.body: Azure Arc extends Azure management to resources outside Azure, such as servers in your own datacenter, Kubernetes clusters in other clouds, and some data services. Arc projects each outside resource into Azure Resource Manager, giving it an Azure resource ID, so you can organise it in resource groups, apply tags, Azure Policy and Azure RBAC, and monitor it with Azure tools while it keeps running where it is. To connect a physical or virtual server, you install the Azure Connected Machine agent on it. Arc-enabled Kubernetes brings outside clusters into one inventory with AKS, and Arc-enabled data services can run Azure SQL Managed Instance on your own Kubernetes infrastructure. Azure VMs do not need Arc because they are already managed by Azure. For example, a company with on-premises Windows servers and Kubernetes in another cloud governs them all from Azure with Arc.

examPoints: A question that describes managing on-premises or other-cloud servers and Kubernetes clusters with Azure Policy, tags and RBAC is testing Azure Arc.
A question about running Azure CLI commands from a computer where nothing can be installed is testing Azure Cloud Shell, which uses the signed-in user's own permissions.
A question about repeatable, declarative deployments of identical environments is testing infrastructure as code with ARM templates or Bicep deployed by Azure Resource Manager.

quiz.q: An administrator is working from a shared library computer where installing software is blocked. She needs to run a few Azure CLI commands right now. What should she use?
choices: Azure PowerShell installed in a local folder on the library computer under her own profile
An ARM template deployment that runs the commands from a storage account in her subscription
Azure Cloud Shell, opened in the web browser with the Azure CLI already available
Azure Arc, after installing the Connected Machine agent on the library computer
quiz.explain: Azure Cloud Shell runs in the browser with the Azure CLI preinstalled and signed in, so nothing is installed locally. Choice D is tempting because Azure Arc manages machines outside Azure, but it brings a server under Azure management; it does not give a person a command shell, and it also needs an agent installed.

quiz.q: A company runs Windows and Linux servers in its own datacenter and wants to apply Azure Policy, tags and Azure RBAC to them alongside its Azure resources. Which service should it use?
choices: Azure Resource Manager templates that redeploy the on-premises servers as new Azure VMs
Azure Arc, which projects the on-premises servers into Azure Resource Manager as resources
Azure Cloud Shell, which connects to the datacenter servers and runs commands on them
Microsoft Entra Domain Services, which joins the datacenter servers to a managed domain
quiz.explain: Azure Arc gives each connected server an Azure resource ID so Azure Policy, tags and RBAC apply while it stays on premises. Choice A is tempting because ARM templates are an Azure management tool, but redeploying as Azure VMs is a migration, and the company wants the servers to stay in its datacenter.

days.recap: Every tool, from the portal and Cloud Shell to the Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell, goes through Azure Resource Manager; ARM templates and Bicep give repeatable deployments, and Azure Arc extends Azure management to resources outside Azure.

days.title: Monitoring: Azure Advisor, Service Health, and Azure Monitor

concepts.heading: Azure Advisor
concepts.body: Azure Advisor analyses your deployed resources and usage and gives personalized best-practice recommendations in five categories: reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence. For example, it can suggest resizing or shutting down underused VMs to save money, adding redundancy to improve reliability, or creating Service Health alerts, which falls under operational excellence. Its security recommendations come from Microsoft Defender for Cloud. Recommendations appear in the portal with the affected resources and suggested actions, and you can create Advisor alerts, filtered by scope and category, to be notified when new recommendations appear. Advisor recommends; it does not change resources by itself. The exam signal is a request for personalized suggestions to improve cost, reliability, security or performance of what is already deployed. Do not confuse it with Azure Monitor, which collects and alerts on telemetry.

concepts.heading: Azure Status, Service Health and Resource Health
concepts.body: Azure Service Health is a family of three views, from widest to narrowest. Azure status is a public web page that gives a global view of Azure health and reports service incidents with broad impact. Service Health is a personalized view in the portal of service issues, planned maintenance, health advisories and security advisories that affect the services and regions you use, and you can create Service Health alerts to be notified. Resource Health shows the health of one specific resource, such as a single VM, and helps you tell whether a problem comes from the Azure platform or from your own actions, with a history of past events. For example, when one VM is unreachable, Resource Health is the first place to check. Exam questions give you a scope, such as all of Azure, my services or one resource, and expect the matching view.

concepts.heading: Azure Monitor: Metrics and Logs
concepts.body: Azure Monitor collects, analyses and acts on telemetry from Azure, other clouds and on-premises resources. Its data platform has two main stores. Metrics are numeric values collected at regular intervals and stored in a time-series database, which suits fast charts and near real-time alerts; Azure resources send platform metrics, such as VM CPU, automatically. Logs are detailed records, such as events and traces, stored in a Log Analytics workspace. To collect logs and performance counters from inside a VM's guest operating system, you install the Azure Monitor Agent and use a data collection rule. The activity log is a separate record of subscription-level operations that shows who created, changed or deleted a resource and when. For example, if a production VM was deleted over the weekend, the activity log shows who did it.

concepts.heading: Log Analytics and KQL
concepts.body: Log Analytics is the tool in the Azure portal for writing and running queries against data in a Log Analytics workspace. Queries use Kusto Query Language (KQL), a read-only language that filters, summarises and joins large volumes of data. The same KQL powers log search alert rules and workbooks, so a query written once can become an alert or a chart. For example, an engineer can search error events from forty VMs in one query instead of logging in to each machine, then count them by computer and hour. Alerts come in three main kinds: metric alerts react to numbers, log search alerts react to the results of a KQL query, such as a specific error message, and activity log alerts react to Azure operations and health events. The exam signal for Log Analytics is querying collected logs across many resources.

concepts.heading: Alerts, Action Groups and Application Insights
concepts.body: An Azure Monitor alert has two parts. The alert rule defines what to watch and the condition, such as CPU above a threshold for a period. The action group defines who is notified and what runs, such as email, SMS, push or voice notifications, or automation such as a webhook, Azure Function, Logic App or runbook. Action groups are reusable across many alert rules. Application Insights is the application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor: it tracks request rates, response times, failures, dependencies and usage for apps running in Azure, on premises or in other clouds. Its availability tests check from several locations that an endpoint responds, even when no real users are active. For example, an online shop can learn about an outage at night instead of the next morning. The exam signal is application performance and availability.

examPoints: A question that asks for personalized recommendations to reduce cost or improve reliability, security or performance is testing Azure Advisor.
A question that names a scope, such as an outage across Azure, issues affecting my subscriptions, or the health of one VM, is testing Azure status versus Service Health versus Resource Health.

A question about querying logs across many resources, alerting with notifications, or tracking app response times is testing Log Analytics with KQL, alert rules with action groups, or Application Insights.

quiz.q: A single VM has stopped responding. The administrator wants to know whether Azure has detected a platform problem with that specific VM. What should she check first?
choices: The Azure status page, which lists all Azure service incidents with broad impact
Azure Advisor, which lists reliability recommendations for every VM in the subscription
Service Health planned maintenance events for all services and regions the company uses
Resource Health for that VM, which shows its current status and past health events
quiz.explain: Resource Health reports the health of one specific resource and whether a problem comes from the Azure platform. Choice C is tempting because Service Health is also personalized, but it reports service-wide issues and maintenance for your services and regions, not the state of one VM.

quiz.q: An admin wants an SMS sent to the on-call engineer whenever any of several alert rules fires, and wants to reuse the same notification setup for future rules. What should be created?
choices: An action group with an SMS notification, attached to each Azure Monitor alert rule
A Log Analytics workspace that stores the phone number of the on-call engineer
An Azure Advisor alert with the operational excellence category for the subscription
A Service Health alert that sends SMS for every service issue in each region
quiz.explain: Action groups define who is notified and what runs, and one action group can be reused by many alert rules. Choice B is tempting because Log Analytics is part of Azure Monitor, but a workspace stores and queries log data; it does not send notifications.

days.recap: Azure Advisor recommends improvements, Service Health tells you about Azure issues at the right scope, and Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs, queries them with KQL, alerts through action groups, and watches apps with Application Insights.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: AZ-900 gives you 45 minutes for the assessment, and you pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Microsoft does not publish the number of questions, so plan your pace by time rather than by a fixed count. The domains are Describe cloud concepts at 25 to 30 percent, Describe Azure architecture and services at 35 to 40 percent, and Describe Azure management and governance at 30 to 35 percent. Besides multiple choice with one or several answers, the exam can include item types such as yes/no series, where you judge several statements about one scenario separately, drag-and-drop items that match or order items, and hotspot items where you choose from a menu or click part of an image. Most questions cover generally available features, so study current product names such as Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Architecture and Services
concepts.body: Many mistakes come from look-alike pairs. Availability zones protect against a datacenter failure inside one region, while region pairs relate two regions in the same geography but do not give automatic failover on their own. Availability sets spread fixed VMs across fault and update domains, while virtual machine scale sets add and remove identical VMs automatically. VPN Gateway sends encrypted traffic over the public internet, while ExpressRoute is a private connection that does not travel over the public internet. LRS keeps copies in one datacenter, ZRS across zones in one region, and GRS or GZRS also copy to a secondary region. Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud directory, while Entra Domain Services adds a managed domain for legacy apps. B2B collaboration serves partners, while an External ID external tenant serves customers. Review days 4 to 8 for any pair that still feels shaky.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Management and Governance
concepts.body: Governance questions often list several tools as choices. Azure RBAC says who can do what, Azure Policy says what may exist and how it must be configured for everyone, resource locks block deletion or changes even by Owners, and Microsoft Purview governs the data itself. The pricing calculator estimates resources you have not deployed yet, while Microsoft Cost Management analyses and budgets real spending, and a budget alerts rather than stopping resources. Azure Advisor recommends improvements, Microsoft Defender for Cloud scores and protects security posture, and Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs and raises alerts. Azure status covers all of Azure, Service Health covers your services and regions, and Resource Health covers one resource. Azure Arc brings outside resources into Azure management, while Azure Resource Manager is the layer every request goes through.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: For every practice question you miss or guess, write down the pair of ideas you confused, such as Azure Policy versus Azure RBAC or Service Health versus Resource Health, and the clue in the stem that should have decided it. Reviewing these pairs is faster than rereading every day, because the same confusions tend to repeat. Spend the most time on Describe Azure architecture and services, the largest domain, unless your log shows a clear weak spot elsewhere. Read each scenario for its deciding phrase, such as before deployment, only from outside the office, prevent deletion, or one specific VM, before looking at the choices, then eliminate choices that solve a different problem. Also watch for retired or old names in distractors, such as Azure AD or Azure Security Center, which current questions replace with Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan
concepts.body: Arrive early or, for an online exam, check your room, webcam and system well before the start time. Read the instructions at the start of the exam and of each section carefully, because they explain how each item type works and whether you can return to questions later. Make a first pass answering what you know and mark uncertain questions for review where review is allowed. With 45 minutes and an unpublished question count, check the timer now and then rather than spending long on one item. In a yes/no series, judge each statement on its own, because several can be yes. For multi-answer questions, choose exactly the number of answers requested. There is no penalty for guessing, because wrong answers simply earn no points, so before you finish make sure every question has an answer.

examPoints: A question that lists Azure RBAC, Azure Policy and resource locks as choices is testing whether you can tell who can act, what may exist, and what cannot be deleted or changed apart.

A question that describes a scope or timing, such as before deployment versus actual spend, or all of Azure versus one resource, is testing the confused pairs pricing calculator versus Cost Management and Azure status versus Resource Health.

quiz.q: A team wants to make sure that developers can create resources, but only of approved VM sizes, and this must apply even to subscription Owners. Which tool enforces the size rule?
choices: Azure RBAC, by giving developers a custom role that can create only small VMs
Azure Policy, by assigning an allowed VM sizes definition with the Deny effect
A ReadOnly resource lock on each resource group where developers deploy VMs
Azure Advisor, by sending cost recommendations whenever a large VM is created
quiz.explain: Azure Policy evaluates resource properties such as VM size and denies noncompliant requests for every caller, including Owners. Choice A is tempting because RBAC controls what developers can do, but roles grant actions on resource types and do not restrict a property such as VM size, and Owners would still have full rights.

quiz.q: A learner keeps mixing up two connectivity services. Which statement correctly separates VPN Gateway from ExpressRoute?
choices: VPN Gateway uses a private connection from a provider, while ExpressRoute sends encrypted traffic over the internet
VPN Gateway connects only virtual networks to each other, while ExpressRoute connects only single user devices
VPN Gateway sends encrypted traffic over the public internet, while ExpressRoute uses a private connection
VPN Gateway and ExpressRoute both require a dedicated circuit from a connectivity provider to work
quiz.explain: VPN Gateway builds encrypted tunnels across the public internet, while ExpressRoute provides a private connection through a connectivity provider. Choice A is tempting because it names both real characteristics, but it swaps them between the two services.

days.recap: AZ-900 is 45 minutes with a scaled pass mark of 700 and an unpublished question count; drill the confused pairs, read each scenario for its deciding clue, and answer every item before submitting.
